exam.subject: General Knowledge
exam.school: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examination (ESSCE) – national
exam.title: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examinations 2021 – General Knowledge (1134)

parts.title: Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: This examination paper contains 100 multiple choice questions only. You must answer all of them. Each question carries one point. There is only one best answer for each question; blacken the letter of your choice on the SCANTRON GENERAL PURPOSE ANSWER SHEET with a pencil.

source.prepared_by: Ministry of Education, Eritrea – ESSCE 2021, General Knowledge, exam code 1134
source.conversion_notes: CamScanner scan (page 1 is an owner's cover note; page 23 is printed twice side by side). Text from tesseract OCR, corrected against the page images; the OCR of pages 4, 6, 8, 9, 13, 15, 17, 19 and 21–23 was badly garbled and those items were re-keyed from the images. Words printed bold and underlined (is not, does not, cannot, is wrong, except, incorrect, most opposite, are not, are true, is true, is less) are marked <u>…</u>. Blanks in items 11, 12, 15 and 91 are shown as ____. Two option-letter misprints are normalised to A–E: item 72 prints its options as A, B, C, B, C and item 97 as A, B, C (left column) and C, D (right column); the original letters are given in those items' review_flag. No figures.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key exists. All answers were solved independently and every fact was checked against reliable general sources (official Eritrean sources such as shabait.com for local facts; encyclopaedias, UN/WHO/agency sites and news archives for world facts). General Knowledge has no textbook: textbook_ref = {source:'general', reference, time_sensitive}. Current-affairs items are answered as correct at the time of the exam (the 2021 ESSCE was sat 12–17 April 2021 under COVID-19 measures, per Eritrea Profile of 10 April 2021; results announced 16 August 2021 – shabait.com); later changes are noted in the explanation and ref note.
exam.textbook_note: No General Knowledge textbook: every textbook_ref is a general-source reference {source:'general', reference, topic, accessed, time_sensitive}.

questions.stem: One of the following ports <u>is not</u> a Red Sea port.
explanation_steps: Suez (Egypt, at the head of the Gulf of Suez), Assab (Eritrea), Port Sudan (Sudan) and Jeddah (Saudi Arabia) all lie on the Red Sea.
Salalah is in southern Oman on the Arabian Sea (Indian Ocean). Answer: E.
tips: Eritrea's own Red Sea ports: Massawa and Assab.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is an Eritrean port on the Red Sea?
explanation_steps: Massawa is Eritrea's main port. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Red Sea; Salalah

questions.stem: Which of the following animals is found only in Australia?
explanation_steps: Kangaroos are marsupials native to Australia (tree kangaroos also live in nearby New Guinea).
Zebras and elephants live in Africa, tigers and pandas in Asia. Answer: B.
tips: Australia's unique animals: kangaroo, koala, platypus, emu.

similar_questions.stem: The giant panda is native to
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Kangaroo

questions.stem: Which of the following could be considered as farmer’s best friend?
explanation_steps: Earthworms burrow and aerate the soil, improve drainage and mix organic matter into humus – they are called the ‘farmer's friend’.
Rats, termites and grain beetles are pests; many birds eat seeds and grain. Answer: C.
tips: Earthworm = natural plough.

similar_questions.stem: Earthworms help crops mainly by
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Earthworm

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases can be prevented by vaccination?
explanation_steps: Yellow fever is a viral disease prevented by a single dose of yellow-fever vaccine.
Diabetes and hypertension are non-infectious; malaria is prevented mainly by bed nets and vector control (a malaria vaccine was only recommended by WHO in October 2021, after this exam). Answer: C.
tips: Vaccines protect against infectious diseases (measles, polio, yellow fever, TB…).

similar_questions.stem: Which disease is prevented by the BCG vaccine?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Yellow fever; Malaria vaccine (RTS,S, recommended 6 Oct 2021)

questions.stem: The smallest continent is
explanation_steps: Australia (Australia/Oceania) is the smallest of the seven continents, about 8.6 million km².
Answer: B.
tips: Largest to smallest: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.

similar_questions.stem: The largest continent is
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Continent

questions.stem: Which of the following statements <u>is not</u> true of a developing country?

options.A: The level of saving is low.
options.B: The economy is dependent on primary sector.
options.C: Large number of people are poor.
options.E: The level of malnutrition is high.

explanation_steps: Developing countries typically have low income and saving, dependence on agriculture/mining, widespread poverty and high malnutrition.
Well-developed health services are a feature of developed countries. Answer: D.
tips: Developing = low income, low saving, primary sector, poverty, weak services.

similar_questions.stem: A typical feature of a developed country is
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Bank / UNDP – characteristics of developing countries

questions.stem: In a right angled triangle, what is the length of the shortest side if the length of the hypotenuse is 65mm and the length of the second longest side is 63mm?
explanation_steps: Pythagoras: a² + b² = c² → a² = 65² − 63² = 4225 − 3969 = 256.
a = √256 = 16 mm. Answer: B.
tips: Difference of squares: c² − b² = (c − b)(c + b).

similar_questions.stem: A right triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm and one side 12 cm. The third side is

textbook_ref.reference: Pythagoras' theorem (school mathematics)

questions.stem: Which of the following components <u>is not</u> part of computer hardware?
explanation_steps: Hardware = physical parts you can touch (memory chips, CPU, keyboard, screen).
Software/programs are instructions, not physical parts. Answer: E.
tips: Hardware = physical; software = programs.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is software?
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Computer hardware; Software

questions.stem: A color blind person <u>cannot</u> differentiate colors between
explanation_steps: The commonest colour blindness is red–green colour blindness (inherited, X-linked, mostly in males).
Answer: A.
tips: Red–green colour blindness is sex-linked – far more common in boys.

similar_questions.stem: Red–green colour blindness is more common in males because the gene is on the
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Color blindness

questions.stem: Ferdinand Magellan is known for

options.A: travelling around the world for the first time.
options.D: travelling around the Cape of Good Hope for the first time.
options.E: travelling to China for the first time.

explanation_steps: Magellan led the Spanish expedition (1519–1522) that made the first circumnavigation of the globe.
He was killed in the Philippines in 1521; Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the voyage in 1522. Columbus reached the Americas (1492); Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope (1488). Answer: A.
tips: Columbus – Americas; Dias – Cape of Good Hope; Vasco da Gama – sea route to India; Magellan – first circumnavigation.

similar_questions.stem: The first European to sail around the Cape of Good Hope was
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Ferdinand Magellan

questions.stem: The natural acid in the human stomach is ____ acid.
explanation_steps: Gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid (HCl), which kills microbes and activates pepsin.
Answer: C.
tips: Stomach = HCl (pH about 1.5–3.5).

similar_questions.stem: Which enzyme is activated by stomach acid to digest proteins?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – Gastric juice

questions.stem: A balloon inflated with ____ gas remains suspended in the air.
explanation_steps: A balloon floats when the gas inside is less dense than air. Helium is much lighter than air (and not flammable, unlike hydrogen).
Oxygen is slightly denser than air; nitrogen almost equal; carbon and phosphorus are solids. Answer: C.
tips: Lighter-than-air gases: helium, hydrogen.

similar_questions.stem: Why is helium preferred to hydrogen in party balloons?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Helium

questions.stem: Which of the following factors <u>does not</u> affect dependency ratio in a country?

options.B: Number of people in the productive age

explanation_steps: Dependency ratio = (children 0–14 + elderly 65+) ÷ working-age population (15–64) × 100.
The number of women as such does not enter the ratio. Answer: E.
Note: the standard (age) dependency ratio does not count disabled people either, so C is also defensible; broader ‘economic dependency’ measures do include them.
tips: Dependency ratio uses AGE groups only.

similar_questions.stem: A country has 400 children, 100 elderly and 1,000 people aged 15–64. Its dependency ratio is

textbook_ref.reference: UN DESA / World Bank – age dependency ratio definition

questions.review_flag: Standard age dependency ratio ignores disability as well as sex; keyed E, C (disabled people) also accepted – teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of African countries are landlocked?
explanation_steps: Rwanda and South Sudan have no coastline.
Kenya, Tanzania and Angola have coasts (Uganda and Ethiopia are landlocked but are paired with coastal states). Answer: D.
tips: Check BOTH countries in each pair.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these countries is landlocked?
explanation_steps: Ethiopia has had no coast since 1993. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Landlocked country; Rwanda; South Sudan

questions.stem: Currently, in Eritrea, individuals are allowed to withdraw cash from their bank accounts any amount up to ____ Nakfa per month.
explanation_steps: Since the 2015 currency exchange, individuals may withdraw at most 5,000 Nakfa in cash per month from their bank accounts (exceptions, e.g. weddings, need a letter from the local administration).
This was the rule at the April 2021 exam (US State Department Investment Climate Statement; BBC, 2019). Answer: D.
tips: Large payments in Eritrea are made by cheque or bank transfer rather than cash.

similar_questions.stem: In Eritrea, the national currency is the
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: US Department of State – 2022 Investment Climate Statement: Eritrea; BBC News (Sept 2019) ‘Eritrea – where ATMs are unknown’
textbook_ref.note: Keyed as at April 2021 (5,000 Nakfa/month). In September 2026 the Bank of Eritrea (Legal Notice 134/2026) added limits on cash held outside banks (25,000 Nakfa for individuals) – check current rules.

questions.stem: Horse power is a unit for measuring the
explanation_steps: Horsepower (hp) is a unit of POWER (rate of doing work); 1 hp ≈ 746 W. It is used for engines and motors.
Speed is measured in km/h or m/s. Answer: B.
tips: SI unit of power = watt; 1 hp ≈ 746 W.

similar_questions.stem: The SI unit of power is the
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Horsepower

questions.stem: The person who invented mobile phone was
explanation_steps: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld mobile-phone call on 3 April 1973.
Bell – telephone; Babbage – mechanical computer; Franklin – lightning experiments; Morse – telegraph code. Answer: D.
tips: Telephone: Bell (1876). Mobile phone: Cooper (1973).

similar_questions.stem: Morse code was developed for the
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Martin Cooper; Mobile telephone

questions.stem: One of the following African countries has three capital cities.
explanation_steps: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial).
Answer: E.
tips: Pretoria – government; Cape Town – parliament; Bloemfontein – courts.

similar_questions.stem: The capital of Nigeria is
explanation_steps: Abuja replaced Lagos in 1991. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – South Africa

questions.stem: Which of the following can pollute the environment?
explanation_steps: Pollution is the introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment: noise pollution, chemical pollution, radioactive pollution and biological pollution (pathogens in water, for example).
Answer: E.
tips: Pollutants can be matter (chemicals, microbes) or energy (noise, heat, radiation).

similar_questions.stem: Untreated sewage in a river is mainly an example of
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Pollution

questions.stem: There are two runners A and B. In one hour, A runs 30 km and B runs 40 km. In three hours, how many more km will be covered by B compared to A?
explanation_steps: B gains 40 − 30 = 10 km each hour.
In 3 hours: 3 × 10 = 30 km. Answer: C.
tips: Relative speed × time.

similar_questions.stem: A car travels 60 km/h and a bus 45 km/h. After 4 hours the car is ahead by

textbook_ref.reference: School arithmetic – speed, distance, time

questions.stem: One of the following child vaccines is given right after birth.
explanation_steps: WHO/EPI schedule: BCG (tuberculosis) is given at birth; measles is given at 9 months; tetanus is given to mothers and later in childhood.
The oral polio ‘zero dose’ (OPV0) is ALSO given at birth in Eritrea's schedule, so E is defensible.
Keyed A; E also accepted.
tips: At birth: BCG + OPV0 (and hepatitis B birth dose in many countries).

similar_questions.stem: The measles vaccine is usually first given at about
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Immunization schedules (BCG and OPV birth dose)

questions.review_flag: Both BCG (A) and the oral polio birth dose (E, OPV0) are given at birth under the Eritrean/WHO schedule. Keyed A, E also accepted.

questions.stem: ‘It takes two hands to clap’, means

options.A: you cannot work with one hand.
options.B: clapping with two hands is victory.
options.C: you can eat with two hands.
options.D: you can work with two hands.

explanation_steps: The saying means that cooperation is needed to achieve something (or that both sides share responsibility for a quarrel).
Of the options, ‘unity is strength’ matches. Answer: E.
tips: Proverbs have a figurative meaning – don't take them literally.

similar_questions.stem: ‘Many hands make light work’ means
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Oxford Dictionary of Proverbs

questions.stem: A bag of oranges weighs 50 kg divided by half of its weight. How much does the bag of oranges weigh in kg?
explanation_steps: Let the weight be w. ‘50 kg divided by half of its weight’: w = 50 ÷ (w/2) = 100/w.
So w² = 100 → w = 10 kg. Check: 50 ÷ 5 = 10. Answer: A.
If the stem is read as the familiar riddle ‘50 divided by a half’ (50 ÷ ½ = 100), the answer would be D.
tips: Translate the words into an equation before calculating.

similar_questions.stem: A number equals 36 divided by the number itself. The positive number is
explanation_steps: x = 36/x → x² = 36 → x = 6. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: School algebra – word problems

questions.review_flag: Ambiguous wording: literal equation w = 50 ÷ (w/2) gives 10 kg (A); the riddle reading ‘50 ÷ ½’ gives 100 kg (D). Keyed A, D also accepted – teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following gases are known as greenhouse gases?
explanation_steps: Greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat: water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, ozone and CFCs.
Hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen and helium are not greenhouse gases; E pairs ozone with hydrogen. Answer: C.
tips: CO₂ (fuels, deforestation) and CH₄ (livestock, rice, landfills).

similar_questions.stem: A major source of methane is
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: IPCC / US EPA – Overview of greenhouse gases

questions.stem: Which of the following place-mineral associations <u>is wrong</u> in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Colluli (Danakil) – potash; Bisha – gold, copper and zinc; Zara – gold (Koka mine); Debarwa – copper (Asmara project).
Adi Rassi (Adi Raesi), near Debarwa, is a COPPER-gold deposit, not iron. Answer: E.
tips: Eritrean mining: Bisha (Zn/Cu/Au), Zara–Koka (Au), Asmara project – Debarwa, Emba Derho, Adi Nefas, Adi Rassi (Cu/Zn/Au), Colluli (potash).

similar_questions.stem: The Colluli project in the Danakil depression is mainly for
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Sunridge Gold – Adi Rassi copper-gold resource (2012), PorterGeo deposit database; Nevsun/Zijin – Bisha; Danakali – Colluli potash

questions.stem: All of the following countries have faced US sanctions, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: The USA has long-standing sanctions programmes on Iran, North Korea and Cuba, and sanctions on Chinese officials and companies (arms embargo since 1989, technology and Xinjiang-related sanctions).
Israel is a close US ally and had not been subject to US sanctions (as at 2021). Answer: E.
tips: Sanctions = economic/political penalties such as trade bans and asset freezes.

similar_questions.stem: The long US trade embargo on Cuba dates from the
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: US Treasury OFAC – sanctions programs list
textbook_ref.note: As at April 2021. In 2024 the US sanctioned some individual Israeli settlers, but not the state of Israel.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a nonfinancial enterprise?
explanation_steps: Financial enterprises deal in money and financial services (banks, insurers, microfinance, investment banks).
A mining company produces physical goods – a non-financial enterprise. Answer: C.
tips: Financial = money services; non-financial = goods and other services.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a financial institution?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: UN System of National Accounts – financial vs non-financial corporations

explanation_steps: Extra paid = 60 − 50 = 10 Nakfa.
Percentage more = 10 ÷ 50 × 100 = 20%. Answer: A.
tips: Percentage change is always on the ORIGINAL value.

similar_questions.stem: A shirt's price rises from 200 to 250 Nakfa. The increase is

textbook_ref.reference: School arithmetic – percentages

tips: Evaluate each option – close distractors (737, 739) catch careless work.

textbook_ref.reference: School arithmetic

questions.stem: Who was the democratic presidential candidate in the 2020 election in the USA?
explanation_steps: Joe Biden was the Democratic nominee (running mate Kamala Harris) and won the November 2020 election; Donald Trump was the Republican candidate.
Bernie Sanders ran in the Democratic primaries but withdrew in April 2020. Answer: D.
tips: Democrats – Biden 2020; Republicans – Trump.

similar_questions.stem: Who became Vice-President of the USA in January 2021?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – United States presidential election of 2020
textbook_ref.note: Biden served as president 2021–2025; Donald Trump won the 2024 election and returned to office in January 2025.

questions.stem: The value of money is directly affected by the
explanation_steps: The value (purchasing power) of money is what it can buy; it moves inversely with the general price level.
When prices rise (inflation), each Nakfa buys less. Answer: C.
tips: Value of money = 1 ÷ price level.

similar_questions.stem: During inflation, the purchasing power of money
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Business and Economics Grade 10 – value of money (p. 40)

questions.stem: Which of the following Eritrean languages belongs to the Nilo-Saharan group?
explanation_steps: Eritrea's nine languages: Semitic (Tigrigna, Tigre, Arabic), Cushitic (Saho, Afar, Bilen, Bidawiet/Hidareb) and Nilo-Saharan (Kunama, Nara).
Answer: A.
tips: Nilo-Saharan = Kunama and Nara (western lowlands).

similar_questions.stem: Tigrigna belongs to which language group?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – Eritrea's nine ethnic groups; Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea: languages

questions.stem: An animal, which has the best long-distance vision, is
explanation_steps: Eagles have extremely sharp eyesight – several times sharper than human vision – and can spot prey from over 3 km away.
Answer: C.
tips: ‘Eagle-eyed’ = having very sharp sight.

similar_questions.stem: Which animal is famous for its very strong sense of smell?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eagle; Eye (vertebrate)

questions.stem: The force, which makes an airplane move forward through the air, is
explanation_steps: Four forces on a plane: thrust (forward, from engines/propellers), drag (backward), lift (upward, from wings) and weight/gravity (downward).
Answer: D.
tips: Thrust vs drag (horizontal); lift vs weight (vertical).

similar_questions.stem: The upward force produced by an aeroplane's wings is
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: NASA Glenn Research Center – Four forces on an airplane

questions.stem: Which of the following words is <u>most opposite</u> in meaning to the word ‘feasible’?
explanation_steps: ‘Feasible’ = possible to do. Practicable, achievable, possible and attainable are synonyms.
The antonym is ‘impossible’. Answer: B.
tips: Find the one option that differs from the rest – often the antonym.

similar_questions.stem: The word most opposite in meaning to ‘scarce’ is
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Oxford Learner's Dictionary – feasible

questions.stem: An animal, which <u>does not</u> give birth, is a
explanation_steps: A mule is the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse. It has an odd number of chromosomes (63), so it is almost always sterile and cannot reproduce.
Horses, donkeys, camels and giraffes are mammals that give birth normally. Answer: B.
tips: Mule = donkey (jack) × horse (mare); sterile hybrid.

similar_questions.stem: A mule's parents are
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Mule

questions.stem: In Eritrea, Toyota and Honda cars can be considered as an example of
explanation_steps: Toyota and Honda cars serve the same purpose, so a buyer can use one instead of the other – substitute goods.
Complementary goods are used together (car and fuel). Answer: D.
tips: Substitutes compete; complements go together.

similar_questions.stem: Cars and petrol are
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Business and Economics Grade 11 – determinants of demand

questions.review_flag: Option C prints ‘complimentary’ for ‘complementary’; does not affect the answer.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is in
explanation_steps: FAO's headquarters is in Rome, Italy.
Geneva – WHO; Paris – UNESCO; Washington DC – World Bank/IMF. Answer: B.
tips: Rome hosts FAO, WFP and IFAD.

similar_questions.stem: The headquarters of UNESCO is in
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: fao.org – About FAO

questions.stem: The Astronomical Unit (AU) refers to the distance between the
explanation_steps: 1 AU = the average Earth–Sun distance ≈ 149.6 million km.
Answer: A.
tips: AU for the solar system; light-year for stars.

similar_questions.stem: A light-year is a unit of
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: IAU / NASA – Astronomical unit

questions.stem: Research finding reports help in
explanation_steps: Research reports supply evidence for decisions and plans, propose solutions to problems and spread (transfer) new knowledge.
Answer: E.
tips: Research → evidence → better decisions, plans and solutions.

similar_questions.stem: The first step of a research process is usually
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: General research-methods texts

questions.stem: Which of the following foods is good for diabetic (high blood sugar) persons?
explanation_steps: Green vegetables are high in fibre and low in sugar and calories, helping control blood glucose.
Cake and soft drinks raise blood sugar quickly; fatty meat raises heart-disease risk. Answer: C.
tips: Diabetes diet: vegetables, whole grains, legumes; limit sugar and saturated fat.

similar_questions.stem: Which drink is best for a person with diabetes?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Diabetes; healthy diet

questions.stem: The World’s tallest building in the year 2020 was
explanation_steps: Burj Khalifa in Dubai (828 m, opened 2010) has been the world's tallest building since 2010.
Shanghai Tower (632 m) is second; the Twin Towers (World Trade Center) were destroyed in 2001; the Sears (Willis) Tower is 442 m. Answer: A.
tips: Burj Khalifa – Dubai, UAE, 828 m.

similar_questions.stem: In which city is the Burj Khalifa?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) – tallest buildings
textbook_ref.note: Burj Khalifa was still the tallest completed building in 2026; the Jeddah Tower (Saudi Arabia), planned to exceed 1,000 m, is under construction.

questions.stem: The animal, which is considered king of the Arctic, is the
explanation_steps: The polar bear is the Arctic's top predator (it hunts seals) and is often called ‘king of the Arctic’.
Lions do not live in the Arctic. Answer: C.
tips: Lion – ‘king of the jungle/savanna’; polar bear – ‘king of the Arctic’.

similar_questions.stem: The main food of polar bears is
explanation_steps: Penguins live in the Antarctic, not the Arctic. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Polar bear

questions.stem: The planet with rings around it is
explanation_steps: Saturn has the large, bright ring system that is easily seen with a small telescope – ‘the ringed planet’.
Strictly, all four giant planets have rings: Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune have thin, faint rings. Venus has none and Pluto is a dwarf planet. The intended answer is D.
tips: All giant planets have rings, but Saturn's are by far the most prominent.

similar_questions.stem: Which planet is the largest in the solar system?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: NASA Solar System Exploration – Saturn; Jupiter; Neptune (rings)

questions.review_flag: Jupiter (A) and Neptune (C) also have (faint) rings; keyed D (Saturn) as the obvious intended answer. Teacher may accept A/C from an informed student.

questions.stem: During the World Cup soccer in 2014, Brazil was hit by a disease outbreak called
explanation_steps: Zika virus spread in Brazil around 2014–2015; researchers first suggested it arrived with visitors to the 2014 FIFA World Cup (later genetic studies date its arrival to about 2013), and the epidemic was recognized in 2015.
Ebola struck West Africa in 2014; coronavirus (COVID-19) began in 2019. Of the options, Zika is the intended answer. Answer: C.
tips: Zika – spread by Aedes mosquitoes; linked to microcephaly in babies.

similar_questions.stem: Zika virus is spread mainly by
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Zika virus; Faria et al. 2016 (Science) on Zika introduction to Brazil

questions.review_flag: Historically imprecise: the Zika epidemic in Brazil was recognized in 2015 (dengue was the main 2014 World Cup concern). Keyed C as the intended answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following inventors is associated with the steam engine?
explanation_steps: James Watt (1736–1819) greatly improved the steam engine (separate condenser, 1769), powering the Industrial Revolution; the unit ‘watt’ is named after him.
Bell – telephone; Faraday – electromagnetic induction; Franklin – electricity experiments; Jefferson – US president. Answer: A.
tips: Watt → steam engine → Industrial Revolution.

questions.stem: Breaking an egg by pressing along its long axis is difficult because the

options.A: force is concentrated at one point.
options.C: eggshell is made up of calcium carbonate.
options.D: pressure is distributed evenly by the arched form of the shell.

explanation_steps: The curved (arch/dome) shape spreads a force applied at the ends over the whole shell, so no single point takes all the stress.
